name: Witzi Episode Posters
overview: Persistent 2:3 episode posters generated from each video
description: Extracts representative frames with Jellyfin's configured media encoder, arranges them into a Witzi-styled portrait poster with randomized borders, stores the JPEG beside the episode video, and registers it as the episode Primary image.

versions.changelog: Serves the theme, pre-paint layer, and browser helper with Jellyfin Web's index.html response instead of writing them into the file. The on-disk edit only reached the browser where the Jellyfin service account could write the web folder, and a Jellyfin Web upgrade replaced the file and took the blocks with it; on such a server, picking a palette changed nothing on screen and the theme still had to come from the branding Custom CSS field. ASP.NET middleware registered with the host now adds the blocks to the response as Jellyfin serves it, reading the configuration per request, so a palette applies on the next page load with nothing written anywhere and no restart. It touches only the web shell request and only a GET returning 200 text/html, and serves the original bytes on any failure. The on-disk write stays available behind a configuration toggle for a server where something other than Jellyfin serves the web folder; while it is off, the startup task clears the blocks releases 1.1.24 and 1.1.25 wrote into index.html.

Restores the injected theme, which Jellyfin Web was overriding wholesale. The plugin wrote the bundle into <head>, but Jellyfin installs its own palette after anything head already carries: MUI writes a :root block of --jf-palette-* values into head as the bundle boots, and themes/<id>/theme.css arrives as a <link> React renders inside #reactRoot. The theme's :root bridge ties with both on specificity and lost every tie, so picking a palette changed nothing on screen. The bundle now goes at the end of <body>, which nothing Jellyfin renders comes after, and an upgrade evicts the copy an earlier release left in head. Jellyfin Web loads its bundles with defer, so the theme is still in place for the first paint. It now also outranks the Custom CSS field, so overrides pasted there need !important.

Serves the theme from Jellyfin Web instead of the Custom CSS field, and stops the page settling in front of the viewer. Jellyfin renders Custom CSS from a React component gated on the branding request, so a theme pasted there cannot apply until after the first paint: the page shows stock Jellyfin colours and landscape home rows, then snaps. The plugin now embeds the six compiled palettes and writes the selected one into index.html beside the pre-paint layer, with a configuration page to pick it and no restart needed to change it. The pre-paint layer also stops revealing content twice: its reveal was a keyframe animation starting from zero, so cards the failsafe had already shown blinked out and faded back in once the helper decided them. Library posters no longer turn a flat colour on hover either, which came from the React card's full-size overlay link inheriting the artwork frame's surface colour.

Stops reporting a poster as failed when Jellyfin is saving the same episode at the same time. Registering artwork rewrites the whole item including its provider rows, and Jellyfin offers no narrower save, so a metadata refresh touching the same episode can still win the race after the retries. The poster file and its sidecar are already installed by that point, and both the local image provider and the post-scan pass select it afterwards, so the write now reports a deferral instead of throwing. Those episodes are counted as registration-deferred rather than failed, and the retry backs off further.

Fixes poster registration failing on PostgreSQL. Saving an episode also writes the shared ItemValues rows for its genres, studios and tags, and Jellyfin looks a row up before inserting it, so two episodes of one series saved at the same time raced to insert the same value and violated the unique index on Type and Value. SQLite never showed this because Jellyfin serializes writes there. Frame extraction stays parallel; the repository write is now serialized and retried when a concurrent library scan writes the same values. Episodes that hit this were reported as failed and kept their previous artwork.

Adds a post-scan pass that restores any Witzi poster a library scan replaced. Whether the local image provider wins Jellyfin merge depends on the library configured image fetcher order, so offering the poster is not on its own a guarantee. The pass runs after every scan, never generates artwork, and records what it restored in witzi-episode-posters-scan.log. Home rows also stop showing the landscape frame before swapping to the poster: card artwork is held back until the helper has settled on an image.

Stops a library scan replacing generated posters with Jellyfin default episode artwork. Installing the poster under the recognized sidecar name only selected it once, and a scan rebuilds that choice from whatever the image providers return. The plugin now contributes the Witzi poster as a local image provider, so it takes part in every refresh, is offered ahead of Jellyfin own episode provider, and marks the Primary image as stored with the media, which suppresses the remote fetch that downloaded a screenshot over it.

Fixes the helper failing to install on servers whose Jellyfin Web directory does not allow new files. Since 1.1.17.0 the index.html replacement was staged as a temporary file beside the target, which needs write access to the directory, while the previous in-place write only needed it on index.html. Staging is still preferred because it cannot leave a truncated web client behind, but a refused staging file now falls back to writing in place and logs a warning.

Builds against the Jellyfin 12.0 RC5 packages; the plugin ABI is unchanged at 12.0.0.0. Newly generated posters now appear without reloading the page, because the browser helper subscribes to the websocket messages Jellyfin already sends and drops only the affected items from its cache when the server reports them changed.

Adopts the theme version number so the plugin and stylesheet ship as one release. Rewrites Jellyfin Web index.html through an atomic rename so an interrupted write can no longer truncate the web client, and injects a pre-paint stylesheet into head so a detail page stops assembling itself in front of the viewer. Fixes a short-read comparison that renamed intact poster sidecars into backups on every run, replaces the per-episode directory scan used to find sidecars, and stops re-reading both posters in full to confirm artwork that has not changed.

Gives every library episode a poster. The scheduled task walks one unpaged episode-id snapshot instead of re-querying by offset, so episodes are no longer skipped when registering artwork reorders the rows still being paged, and episodes that share a multi-episode video file build their poster once instead of racing for it.
Caps poster generation at four concurrent episode workers regardless of the server image-encoding setting, preventing large AV1 batches from exhausting available memory or process threads.

Writes poster-generation diagnostics to a dedicated Witzi log with explicit per-episode skip and failure reasons plus a final outcome summary, keeping detailed FFmpeg and poster messages out of Jellyfin's main log.

Keeps Witzi artwork selected after Jellyfin metadata refreshes by installing it under the provider-recognized episode Primary filename, while preserving conflicting local sidecars as recoverable backups and reusing existing Witzi output without rerunning FFmpeg.

Generates dedicated Witzi sidecars, reuses existing Witzi artwork without rerunning FFmpeg, replaces a different Primary registration without deleting its file, and processes episodes concurrently using Jellyfin's Parallel image encoding limit.

Optimizes the embedded browser helper by processing only affected cards, backdrops, playback containers, and detail layouts; supports Jellyfin's modern image updates; and updates the installed helper in place without reordering other plugin injections.

Limits generation to episodes and checks registered Primary artwork plus every Jellyfin-recognized episode sidecar before starting FFmpeg, preserving existing posters without regenerating or overwriting them.
Precisely aligns each newly composed detail ribbon to its poster with one initial rendered-edge adjustment while preserving normal scrolling and avoiding scroll-time style updates.
Builds the detail ribbon as the view appears, restores normal page scrolling, removes scroll-time geometry corrections, and adds bottom spacing to item details.
Fixes Jellyfin 12 startup by waiting for user Custom CSS before activating the embedded helper and reserving initialization against older injected copies.
Installs the embedded Witzi browser helper into Jellyfin Web at startup, keeps detail content inside the real ribbon, uses the full detail-page width, and improves horizontal row controls.
Rebuilt for the Witzi v1.1.5 release with GPU-first frame extraction, randomized frame-border colors, and Jellyfin 12.0 ABI compatibility.
Randomize each generated poster's three frame-border colors using distinct colors from the Witzi/Catppuccin palette.
Initialize Jellyfin plugin metadata correctly and prefer hardware-accelerated FFmpeg frame decoding with an automatic software fallback.
Remove the direct SkiaSharp dependency and expose poster generation as a manual-only Library scheduled task.
Initial Jellyfin 12 ABI release.
